newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Interstate eyeing hotel mgmt co. [CORRECTED 19:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Interstate eyeing hotel mgmt co. [CORRECTED 19:40 GMT]

text.p: Interstate Hotels Co, the 30-year-old company that went public last June, intends to continue its luxury-hotel buying spree and also has set its sights on acquiring a hotel management company, Chief Financial Officer J. William Richardson (corrects name throughout from W. Thomas Parrington) said in an interview.

"We are a buyer of hotels in the luxury, upscale segment, and that is where we want to remain. We own hotels all over the United States and we do not have a particular geographic preference. We look at the opportunties as they come up," Richardson told Reuters.
"We are also looking for a management company. There is going to be further consolidation in this area," he said.

"We have been on a strategy of buying individual hotels because when portfolios come up for sale, the bidding often gets too heated. You often get assets you don't want and end up overpaying. But we do not preclude buying packages of hotels," Richardson said.
He declined comment on acqusitions or other transactions that might be in the works.

Interstate is among a handful of lodging companies that is aggressively buying luxury hotels, adding to inventory that enjoys "all-time high occupancy" while remaining cheaper to buy rather than construct because of several waves of overbuilding since the mid-1980s, Richardson said.
Also in the hunt for upper-tier hotels are Host Marriott Corp, Starwood Lodging Trust and Patriot American Hospitality Inc, among others.
